clue.text: Bone buried in barrow at the point of death

indicators.note: something buried lies inside the ground, so the bone goes within the barrow

parts.note: a barrow is an ancient burial mound
a rib is a bone of the chest

explanation.surface: An archaeologist finds a bone in a burial barrow belonging to someone who was dying.
explanation.definitionFit: Moribund describes someone close to dying, on the brink of expiring.

clue.text: Fashionable second course

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second ('half a mo')
a dish is a course of a meal

explanation.surface: A trendy follow-up dish served at a restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: Modish is a synonym for stylish and in vogue.

clue.text: Wrapped in material, case of Soave shut up again

indicators.note: the outer letters of Soave are enclosed by the word for material

parts.note: material in the sense of physical, tangible: real

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A bottle of Soave wine is wrapped in cloth and sealed again.
explanation.definitionFit: To reseal is to close something up once more after it was opened.

clue.text: Footwear on pirate

parts.note: a boot is footwear
in cricket the on side is also called the leg side

explanation.surface: A pirate's boot, as if describing his costume.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side of the field is also called the on side, so 'on' gives LEG.
explanation.definitionFit: To bootleg is to copy or sell goods illegally, the same as to pirate them.

clue.text: Keats' almost sensational feeling about a subject of one of his odes

definitions.text: subject of one of his odes

parts.note: nigh means nearly, almost

indicators.note: the tingle goes around the letter a

parts.note: a tingle is a physical sensation

explanation.surface: Keats nearly thrilled by the subject of one of his odes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keats'' sets up 'his', so the definition reads as the subject of one of Keats's odes: Ode to a Nightingale.
explanation.definitionFit: Keats wrote the famous Ode to a Nightingale, about the songbird.

clue.text: Tool is grabbed by team when water cut off

indicators.note: the word 'is' is held inside what is left of the team
the water is removed from the team's name

parts.note: Chelsea is a London football club
the sea is a body of water

explanation.surface: A football team loses a tool when the water supply is cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: Chelsea is a London football club, not a word for a team in general; 'water' is a synonym to remove from it, not a supply.
explanation.definitionFit: A chisel is a cutting tool used on wood or stone.

clue.text: Audio equipment offering choice of call, character phoning home

parts.note: when a coin is tossed, one calls heads or tails
E.T., the film alien, famously says 'phone home'

explanation.surface: Kit that lets you choose whom to call, like an alien ringing home.
explanation.definitionFit: A headset is a pair of headphones, often with a microphone, for listening.

clue.text: Cash fine

definitions.meaning: ... also means excellent, of high quality

explanation.definitionFit: Sterling names the British currency and also means admirable or first-rate.

clue.text: Ability to read story filled with smut, ultimately somewhat indecorous

indicators.note: the story has a letter put inside it

parts.note: a story can mean a lie ('don't tell stories')

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of smut is used

parts.note: racy means a little risqué or improper

explanation.surface: A smutty story with some indecent bits, testing whether one can read.
explanation.definitionFit: Literacy is the skill of reading and writing.

clue.text: Shift first of ice blocking dogsled on the move

indicators.note: the letter stands inside the rearranged dogsled, blocking it
moving letters around signals a rearrangement of dogsled
takes the first letter of ice

explanation.surface: Ice gets in the way of a moving dog sled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the move' rearranges DOGSLED and I (first of ice) goes inside after the D.
explanation.definitionFit: To dislodge something is to move it out of position.

clue.text: Clear butter quantity probed by all fingers and thumbs, say?

indicators.note: the number pokes into the pat, inside it

parts.note: a pat of butter is a small portion
eight fingers and two thumbs make ten digits

explanation.surface: Clarified butter poked by someone clumsy, all fingers and thumbs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All fingers and thumbs' normally means clumsy; here it counts them: ten.
explanation.definitionFit: Patent as an adjective means obvious or plain to see.

clue.text: Red little mark, fancifully?

parts.note: a scar is a mark on the skin
-let is a suffix meaning small, as in piglet

explanation.surface: A small red mark, imaginatively described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancifully' admits the joke: a small scar would be a 'scarlet', as a small pig is a piglet.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarlet is a vivid shade of the colour.

clue.text: Shark, teeth like efficient razors, all initially going after fish with tail ripped off

indicators.note: the initials come after the shortened fish
the final letter of the fish is removed

parts.note: huss is a name for dogfish sold as food in Britain

indicators.note: the first letter of each of those four words

explanation.surface: A shark with razor-sharp teeth chasing a fish and tearing off its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shark' looks like the fish of the surface, but it is a swindler. Huss is the British fishmonger's name for dogfish.
explanation.definitionFit: A shark in slang is a con man or swindler, the same as a hustler.

clue.text: Soldier on manoeuvres nearing the welcoming capital in Havana

indicators.note: the rearranged letters take in a letter, welcoming it inside
troops on manoeuvres move about, so the letters of nearing the are rearranged
the capital letter of Havana, its first

explanation.surface: A soldier on exercises approaching the Cuban capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldier on' reads as a soldier on manoeuvres; it is the verb phrase meaning persist.
explanation.definitionFit: To hang in there is to persevere despite difficulty.

clue.text: Drink: good inn can do it on the rocks

indicators.note: wrecked or broken up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A good pub can serve a drink over ice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the rocks' suggests ice in the drink but signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A gin and tonic is a classic mixed alcoholic cocktail.

clue.text: German writer beginning on scarier, terrifying tale

indicators.note: takes the first letter of scarier

parts.note: a chiller is a frightening story

explanation.surface: A German author starts on an even scarier horror story.
explanation.definitionFit: Friedrich Schiller was a German poet and playwright.

clue.text: Current crossed by lads aboard craft — lighter?

indicators.note: the letters go on board, inside, the craft

parts.note: art is a craft or skill

indicators.note: the lads cross over the current, so it sits within them

parts.note: sons are lads, boys
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Boys on a boat crossing a current, perhaps in a lighter barge.
explanation.walkthrough: A lighter is a barge, which suits the boating surface; the definition means someone who lights fires.
explanation.definitionFit: An arsonist deliberately sets fires, so is one who lights them, playfully a lighter.

clue.text: Statesman's concern with extra weight carried?

definitions.meaning: a business, a concern, or a civic body a statesman might run
old slang for a pot belly

explanation.definitionFit: Corporation means both a business enterprise and, humorously, a paunch or large stomach.

clue.text: Equines working a long time, guzzling last of water

parts.note: a machine that is on is working

indicators.note: the long time takes in a letter, as if drinking it

parts.note: ages means a long time

indicators.note: the final letter of water

explanation.surface: Horses working for hours, drinking water.
explanation.definitionFit: Onagers are wild asses of Asia, members of the horse family.

clue.text: Author in front standing to pen new book

indicators.note: the reversed van encloses the other letters, as a pen holds animals
in a down clue, standing up means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: the van is the front, as in vanguard

indicators.note: new signals a fresh arrangement of book

explanation.surface: A writer at the front, standing to write a new book.
explanation.walkthrough: VAN stood up (read upwards in a down clue) is NAV, which holds BOKO, a rearranged BOOK.
explanation.definitionFit: Vladimir Nabokov was the Russian-American novelist who wrote Lolita.

clue.text: Use force to get a compliment

indicators.note: the forcing word gets the letter a, taking it inside

parts.note: to prise is to lever open by force

explanation.surface: Using force to extract a compliment from someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Praise is approval or admiration expressed, a compliment.

clue.text: Stuck in branches, treetop close, perhaps?

indicators.note: the answer is stuck within these two words, spanning them

explanation.surface: Something caught in the branches near the top of a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close' looks like an adjective meaning near; it is a noun, a cul-de-sac.
explanation.definitionFit: A close is a type of residential road, so it is an example of the answer.

clue.text: Cut off, one thus gone

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
so means thus, in this way
late means dead, departed

explanation.surface: Someone cut off, thus gone.
explanation.definitionFit: To isolate is to separate or detach something from others.

clue.text: Shabby material covering plain silk

indicators.note: the shabby stuff surrounds, covers, the plain word

parts.note: tat is cheap tasteless goods
bare means plain, unadorned

explanation.surface: Cheap fabric covering a plain silk.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabaret is a durable striped fabric of silk used for upholstery.

clue.text: Wait in back of limo, opening some American wine?

indicators.note: the letter opens up the American measure, splitting it apart

parts.note: a liter, the US spelling of litre, is a quantity of wine

indicators.note: the back of something is its rear end, so only the final letter of limo is used

explanation.surface: Waiting in the back of a limousine, opening some Californian wine.
explanation.definitionFit: To loiter is to hang about, lingering idly.

clue.text: Brass bar as plunger?

parts.note: brass and neck both mean cheek, impudence
a bar is a line, as in a stripe

explanation.surface: A brass rod used as a plunger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plunger' sounds like a sink tool, but a plunging neckline dips low.
explanation.definitionFit: A low-cut neckline is said to plunge, so one could fancifully call it a plunger.

clue.text: Setter messed up further attempt at passing

indicators.note: jumbled, so the letters of setter are rearranged

explanation.surface: The setter blundered and must take another exam.
explanation.definitionFit: A retest is a second sitting of an exam or trial for those who failed.

clue.text: Fights during preliminary race, most serious

indicators.note: the fights happen within the race, inside it

parts.note: a heat is a qualifying round of a race
vies means competes, struggles

explanation.surface: Clashes during a qualifying race, of the gravest kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Heaviest in the sense of weightiest, the most grave or important.
